venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner never lets you sit. White never lets the tackle get a clean count. FAU still lived on the throw they were given.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — combined condensed tape + GNFP Week 2 film pass. Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: The offense is a numbers game with Baugh as the chip. The defense is a lever with Woods on it. The hitch is what ninety snaps cost when nobody sits in the window.

offense.body:
You cannot put a card on this offense. That is the point.

Faulkner is not installing a system you can script against. He is asking a new question before you finish the last one. Same first step, different answer. The backside is live — they do not need a new call to go the other way. Load the play side and they throw the hitch Brown ran in for 49. Step with the pullers and the ball goes the other way, to the three, and Brown is already in space. Come down for Baugh and the line is in a pass set and Abrams is gone 63. Stay home and Baugh hits the pull from 12, or he takes the 61 when the whole stadium knows.

That is one idea. The costume keeps changing.

They split the field and stack Brown and Wilson behind the two in front. FAU kept extra in the box because they have seen Baugh. Now you are one-on-one with a lot of grass. One miss is a house call. The 49 lives there. So does the rest of Brown’s night — the screen, the 14, the 33. He is not a gadget. They load one side, motion, the strength moves, and they can still go weak. FAU’s count was late all night. Unbalanced is not window dressing. It is the numbers game.

The pull is the lie and the truth. Tackles sell counter, interior three leave, ball goes with the three — Brown, later Clark, and on Clark’s 10-yard score the big people are already down the field. When the pull is real, Baugh walks into it. When they need a yard, nobody leaves — sneak, Philo from the 3.

They will also pull the tackle on a pass. The end is paid to rush the passer. Instead that tackle leaves like the run is going the other way. Honor it and the front slows down without getting blocked. Chase the quarterback and you are empty. Week one they planted that look more than they cashed it. They will hand it out of the same picture. Remember it.

Pistol showed up once in the opening script — run, then Wilson sitting under the zone for 19. One look. Not the offense. Wilson moved the chains all night. He sits where you leave him.

Philo ran the operation. In and out. Eyes down when the rush came. Climb, slide, still find somebody. He does not have to be the hero. Stockton finished a ball that was a touch late and walked it in from 11. Abrams was on time; lead him a step and it is a walk-in. The pick is Mays. Sweeney was sitting. When Philo holds it, the play dies.

Baugh is the night. Fourteen for 160, three rushing scores, the 61. There were snaps FAU filled every gap — the right call, run blitz, dead — and he still ripped it or scored. That is not scheme winning those snaps. That is the best player in the building. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven on him. Wide splits make that a nightmare. Duke Clark is the change of pace. They will not run Baugh thirty times.

The line is not road-grading anybody. They are clean — no hold parade, no false-start night, the late shift that wrecked them last year does not get them. They are also not getting to the second level with quickness. Outside zone they cannot run yet. Faulkner will still put it on film so you have to honor the edge. His hack: leave people unblocked on purpose so this line is not asked to win every one-on-one. The high snaps are technique. Sumrall already tied them to a run-block that messes with Moore’s hands. The one that lost twenty inside the five is the one that can lose a real game. The keep when Sledge crashes and is still there — design was sound. They lost the snap.

Downfield they block like they mean it. Turns ten into thirty. Micah Jones late blows up the end, then the next guy, and they throw him the last one. That is not a coincidence. Get the big people in front of a skill player. Same family as Clark’s score.

What Saturday was: a coordinator who flexes to what you are weak at, a back you cannot tackle if the box is honest, and a quarterback who ran the building. What to clean is the snap, the Sledge keep, and the ball off Mays. The rest is a headache you have to prepare for.
bullets: Same first step, different answer. The backside is live.
Wide splits and the stack: extra for Baugh, or grass outside for Brown.
The pull is the costume — screen, punch, or a pass the end has to honor.
Baugh is the night. Clean the snap, the Sledge keep, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
An air-raid lives on the short throw until you climb and take it away. Everybody knows that. Florida left that throw on the grass.

Corners off. Backers not fanning into the hitch. You showed them something before the snap and then you gave them the first read. Ninety snaps. They were 10-of-13 on third at one point. Henry and Valsin took what was given. Sumrall said it out loud: third-and-1, you cannot play nine yards off. That happened. That is the tax. White will live with five-to-eight if they tackle. They did not tackle enough of it, and nobody sat in the window, so it became a night.

He still has a real idea. Odd fronts. Movement. Woods is the lever. On third down White moves him. On the ball, Woods is the edge. Off the ball, the edge belongs to somebody else and Woods is coming from a different spot. The tackle never gets a clean count. Mix it. Often. Not a statue, and not a park-him-there plan.

When Veltkamp holds it, that idea pays. Shade front. Coleman opens to the middle, sells the hole, the ball goes outside, Coleman is already back. That pick is a bait. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. He tips the next one. Johnson goes up and gets it. Same family. Bett later knives the keep at the 1. Ball out. Johnson falls on it. McCloud takes fourth-and-2. The rush finally finishes. Safeties were the clean room — Coleman, Thornton. The nickel played a real night and lost the fade once with no help over the top. That fade is the other side of sitting off. Valsin, 20. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

What leaked is the stuff they agreed to give, plus the jobs inside it. The pile at the 1 — front was right, they lost the yard. The edge leaving and Veltkamp walking in from 7. Woods is the lever, and when he chases, FAU ran at him. Keep him home. The later tape is more four-down, still off, still one-high. That is how you kill the explosive. That is also how the hitch and the fade stay alive.

They were ready for the tempo. They were not staring at the sideline while it snapped. Communication was not the spring fear. Veltkamp is a real small-school quarterback — touch, nimble, he will hurt you if you let him throw it now. Sumrall called the defense atrocious at times because ninety snaps and those fourth downs are what you get when the short game is free.

Sit on the hitch. Keep the edge when the quarterback pulls it. Mix Woods. Make him hold it. Coleman already showed you what that looks like.
bullets: Woods is the lever. Mix him. The tackle never gets a clean count.
The hitch is the tax because nobody sat in the window. Ninety snaps.
Coleman sells middle, takes outside. Johnson is the same family.
Clean the pile, the edge, and the fade. Sit on the short throw.

specials.body: The drive stalls. They take the points. Durkin from 53. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt is how the second Florida score starts.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt sets up the short field.

Wide splits and the stack: extra for Baugh, or grass outside for Brown.
White moves Woods so the tackle cannot count. The hitch is the tax because nobody sat in the window.
When he holds it, Coleman and Johnson are the wait. Clean the pile, the edge, and the fade.

nextWeek.look: They will throw it short and keep it. Sixkiller is the show — he throws it and he is their leading runner. Florida will still run Baugh and dress the line. White has to sit on the hitch and keep Woods’ edge home when the quarterback pulls it.
